Action Plan:
1. Acute diarrhoea & vomiting – arrange urgent face-to-face clinic appointment today for:
   • Hydration status check (including vitals and clinical assessment)  
   • Provision of stool sample pot and same-day dispatch for microscopy, culture & sensitivity (±PCR)  
   • Review need for targeted therapy once results available
2. Ongoing hydration advice – continue oral re-hydration salts (ORS) every few minutes in small sips; maintain bland diet (toast/biscuits), avoid fruit, vegetables, milk, alcohol.
3. Safety-net – if worsening vomiting, reduced urine output, inability to keep fluids down, severe abdominal pain, or red-flag signs (blood in stool/black stool, persistent fever) → attend local Emergency Department (A&E) immediately or call service back.
4. Administrative – patient to phone support line to book same-day clinic slot; clinician to document results and follow-up plan once stool test returned.
5. Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
• Reason for consult: 3-day history of profuse loose/watery diarrhoea with vomiting, subjective fever, peri-umbilical abdominal pain.  
• Frequency: ≥4 bowel motions today (“lost count” overall).  
• Vomiting: everything taken orally (water, tea, ORS). Last vomit ≈2 h before call (after breakfast).  
• Fever: feels “boiling”; no thermometer reading.  
• Pain: peri-umbilical, sore to touch, colicky, coincides with urge to defecate.  
• Urination: last void 1 h ago; color unknown.  
• No blood in stool or urine.  
• Exposure: brother with similar illness; reports school outbreak. No recent travel.  
Past Medical/Surgical Hx: none significant; no previous abdominal disease or surgeries.  
Medications: vitamin D (dose/route/frequency not documented); occasional ibuprofen for dysmenorrhoea (dose/route/frequency not documented).  
Allergies: not documented.  
Social: Non-smoker; occasional alcohol (“a pint from time to time”). Lives with mother and brother. Graphic designer; worked from home today due to illness.  
Gyn: Last menstrual period 2 weeks ago; not on contraception; not sexually active currently.

Objective:
• Remote consultation – no physical examination performed, no vitals available.

Investigations (planned): Stool MCS (±viral PCR) to rule out bacterial gastroenteritis; hydration assessment at clinic (vitals, possible bloods—U&E/FBC—if indicated).

Assessment & Plan:

1. Acute diarrhoea & vomiting  
   - Assessment: Suspected infectious gastroenteritis (likely viral vs food-borne bacterial).  
   - Differential: Norovirus/rotavirus; bacterial food poisoning (Campylobacter, Salmonella, Shigella, E. coli).  
   - Investigations: Stool MCS/PCR; consider bloods if clinically indicated at clinic review.  
   - Treatment: Continue ORS; bland diet; avoid irritant foods; possible targeted antibiotics only if stool confirms bacterial pathogen; consider anti-emetic if vomiting persists (not yet prescribed).

2. Risk of dehydration  
   - Assessment: Mild dehydration risk (still passing urine).  
   - Investigations: Hydration review in clinic (vital signs, capillary refill, mucous membranes, possible serum electrolytes).  
   - Treatment: Reinforce ORS regimen (frequent small sips); monitor urine output; escalate to ED if unable to hydrate or develops red-flags.

Quality checks:
● Missing expected elements: allergy status not elicited; detailed medication doses/frequencies not documented; no objective vitals/physical exam recorded.  
● Internal conflicts: none noted.  
● Transcript quality: clear audio; minor pauses, otherwise intelligible.
